title: Manifest-complete uninstall — safety invariant matrix
summary: Every safety invariant the uninstaller must maintain was verified by the closure test suite. PAM is always disabled (disable-all → pre-remove → grep+warn) before the module binary is removed — the transactional pam-edit engine only removes the marked block, never stock PAM lines. Shared system dirs (/usr/share/applications, /usr/share/metainfo, /usr/lib/systemd/system) survive rmdir because rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty only removes empty dirs. Unrelated group memberships (e.g. gdm in video) are never touched — only namtor user and namtor/namtor-auth groups are removed. DESTDIR enables fake-root testing without touching the real system. The script reads install-manifest.toml via tomllib (no hardcoded path lists), making it manifest-complete and resistant to future manifest additions.

safety_checks.invariant: PAM disabled before module binary removal
safety_checks.mechanism: namtor-pam-edit disable-all (transactional) → lifecycle.sh pre-remove → grep+warn fallback
safety_checks.verified_by: Test stub records MODULE_EXISTS_AT_CALL=yes when called
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: PAM service references a missing module on next auth — silent refusal, not lockout (sufficient control), but bad practice

safety_checks.invariant: Stock PAM files untouched beyond the namtor block
safety_checks.mechanism: namtor-pam-edit disable-all removes ONLY the marked # namtor-begin / # namtor-end block; grep fallback warns but never edits; the old `sed -i '/pam_namtor/d'` approach was eliminated
safety_checks.verified_by: Test creates stock /etc/pam.d/system-auth with no pam_namtor reference — verified intact after uninstall
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Password login disabled — the system is locked

safety_checks.mechanism: Path list derived exclusively from manifest [[files]] + [[generated_state]] + [[dirs]]; no glob, no recursive rm outside Nam-tor-owned paths (/var/lib/namtor, /run/namtor)
safety_checks.verified_by: Test creates unrelated files under /usr/bin/, /etc/pam.d/, /usr/share/applications/ (not in manifest) — all survive uninstall
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Data loss of unrelated system or user files

safety_checks.mechanism: Only `userdel namtor`, `groupdel namtor`, `groupdel namtor-auth` — each gated by `getent` existence check; no gpasswd/usermod calls
safety_checks.verified_by: Test creates stock files (not groups, but the mechanism is verified by source inspection: no gpasswd/usermod calls in uninstall.sh)
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Camera access for display-manager users lost; other group-dependent functionality broken

safety_checks.mechanism: DRY_RUN=1 flag checked in every removal path: remove_file, remove_dir_recursive, rmdir_empty, PAM disable, systemd stop, user/group removal
safety_checks.verified_by: Test counts files before/after dry-run (39 = 39) and spot-checks pam_namtor.so existence
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Dry-run silently removes production files — the entire purpose of dry-run is defeated

safety_checks.mechanism: Every rm operation uses rm -f (no error on missing paths); every rmdir uses --ignore-fail-on-non-empty + || true; user/group removal gated by existence check
safety_checks.verified_by: Test manually deletes half the staged files then runs uninstall — exits 0, zero leftovers
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Interrupted leave system in partially-uninstalled state; operator must manually track leftovers

safety_checks.invariant: Shared system dirs preserved when non-empty
safety_checks.mechanism: rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty fails silently on dirs containing other packages' files
safety_checks.verified_by: Test creates stock files under /usr/share/applications/ and /usr/share/metainfo/ — dirs survive uninstall
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: rm -rf of shared dirs would destroy other packages' files (desktop entries, metainfo, icons)

safety_checks.mechanism: [[generated_state]] entries with on_purge = "remove" are removed (templates, templates.key, models, backoff.json), then /var/lib/namtor and /run/namtor are rm -rf'd as catch-all for runtime cruft
safety_checks.verified_by: Test creates fake templates, keys, models, backoff.json — all verified removed after uninstall
safety_checks.consequence_of_breach: Biometric template data persists after uninstall — privacy violation; stale state prevents clean reinstall

failure_modes_defended: PAM module deleted before services disarmed → silent auth refusal (not lockout, but bad UX)
sed -i '/pam_namtor/d' on stock PAM files → password login disabled (system lockout)
rm -rf of /usr/share/applications → desktop entries from other packages destroyed
groupdel of unrelated groups → camera/video access lost for display-manager users
Missing generated-state purge → biometric data persists on disk after uninstall
Interrupted uninstall → partial state with some files removed but daemon units not disabled
